newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan gold rates seen down on higher imports.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan gold rates seen down on higher imports.

text.p: Pakistan gold rates are likely to fall this week on higher imports as a gold import monopoly comes to an end, dealers said on Monday.
Gold fell to 4,962 rupees per 10 grams of 24 carat on Sunday, a four-month low, from 4,971 on Thursday, compared to 5,082 on January 19 and a high of 5,228 on January 13.
One dealer said rates were likely to ease on higher imports after the government allowed two more companies to import gold, ending the monopoly enjoyed by ARY Traders since early 1995.
Another dealer said lower prices reflected a steep fall in bullion markets abroad, where gold fell below $350 an ounce.

The government has authorised Karachi-based M.R. Rahim and Lahore-based Mohammad Al-Ramzan to import gold and silver, alongside ARY Traders. The importers will pay duty of $1.40 per tola (11.664 grams) for gold and $2 per kilo for silver.
One dealer said the competition was likely to push gold prices below 4,500 rupees per 10 grams. Silver prices, unchanged last week, were also likely to dip.
